description: Conformance cases for apple-app-site-association semantics. Any implementation claiming to evaluate AASA should pass all of them.

statuses.decided: Apple does not state it; blazingly-aasa chose a reading. See docs/parity.md.
statuses.oracle: Checked against Apple's swcutil and recorded in conformance/oracle. The strongest evidence available short of shipping an app.

matching.name: apple/components/missing-query-fails
matching.note: Apple states this URL does not match.

matching.name: apple/components/missing-path-fails
matching.note: Apple states this URL does not match.

matching.name: defaults/absent-fragment-matches-star
matching.note: Apple's own example relies on `#: *` matching a URL with no fragment.

matching.name: order/reversed-makes-exclude-unreachable
matching.note: First match wins, so the later exclude never runs.

matching.name: query/item-without-equals-is-empty
matching.note: Apple does not document valueless query items.

matching.name: query/repeated-name-matches-any-occurrence
matching.note: Apple does not document which occurrence wins.

matching.name: query/non-string-predicate-never-matches
matching.note: Apple documents only string patterns here.

matching.name: encoding/default-compares-encoded-url
matching.note: Apple says only that percentEncoded indicates 'whether URLs are percent-encoded'. This crate reads the default as comparing the pattern against the URL component exactly as written.

matching.name: encoding/default-rejects-decoded-pattern
matching.note: The corollary of the default: a pattern written with literal characters does not match an encoded URL unless percentEncoded is turned off.

matching.name: encoding/false-decodes-the-url
matching.note: With percentEncoded false this crate decodes the URL rather than encoding the pattern, because encoding a pattern containing * and ? is not well defined.

matching.name: encoding/encoded-slash-is-not-a-separator
matching.note: %2F stays encoded under the default, so a rule written as /a/b does not accept /a%2Fb. This is the security-relevant half of the percentEncoded choice.

matching.name: encoding/decoding-erases-the-slash-distinction
matching.note: The other half: turning decoding on makes /a%2Fb indistinguishable from /a/b. Worth knowing before setting percentEncoded false on a rule that guards something.

matching.name: encoding/non-ascii-decoded
matching.note: Decoding lets a pattern contain literal non-ASCII text, which is the main reason to set percentEncoded false at all.

matching.name: substitution/literal-text-is-not-the-variable
matching.note: A pattern of $(food) must not compare as the literal text $(food).

matching.name: substitution/region-uses-iso-not-prose
matching.note: $(region) is generated from Foundation's isoRegionCodes rather than transcribed, so the list Apple points at wins over the examples in Apple's prose.

matching.name: substitution/region-rejects-uk
matching.note: Apple's prose lists UK, but isoRegionCodes contains GB and not UK.

matching.name: substitution/class-folds-when-case-insensitive
matching.note: Predefined variables are lists of strings, so folding applies to them too.

matching.name: legacy/details-as-dictionary
matching.note: The oldest association-file form; key order is undefined so it is evaluated sorted.

matching.name: host/other-host-never-matches
matching.note: The file does not carry its own domain; the caller supplies it.

matching.name: host/empty-domain-skips-the-check
matching.note: An empty domain means 'do not check the host'. That is this crate's API, not an Apple behaviour: swcutil requires -d, so the oracle cannot speak to it.
